title: I'm trying to build a 3D State-Space Model for BTC (Using Orbital Mechanics / Physics-based Quant Framework) Advice from multiple angles would be appreciated!
author: South-Ad2566

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: orbital mechanics works because the system conserves energy and the forces don't change when you look at them. price has neither, so the physics ends up as a fancy set of free parameters. I'd check it against a plain random walk before anything else.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: np. if you build it anyway, keep the last year out of the fitting entirely and only look at it once at the end.

replies.author: South-Ad2566
replies.body: I'm only attached to the things that produce verified results, this is just a thought that i followed to see if it would bear fruit. Really I'm only interested in making a working algorithm that's profitable

replies.author: South-Ad2566
replies.body: I have several pieces of a working algorithm I'm still learning how to string it together, it doesn't help that my AI is still in development. I had one friend that recommended looking into ema ribbon, squeeze indicator, and MW pattern trading. Have any advice?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then the random walk comparison is your fastest verdict. if the model can't beat shuffled returns on data it never saw, you have the answer in an afternoon.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: The 3D view is a nice way to see how price, momentum and volume move together. The real test is whether a trading rule built on it beats a simple baseline, like a basic moving average rule or random entries, out of sample and after fees. One thing to watch is that any normalizing or scaling uses only data available at that moment, since scaling over the whole visible window quietly uses the future. A physics comparison can be a useful way to think, but markets don't have to follow it, so I'd let the data decide. Cymetica's Backtest Labs can run a rule on past data with a fee setting and a held out stretch.
